# Mixed interface default forwarding

A package final child of a named static parent forwards reference and scalar
arguments to a direct interface default. The parent and four direct interfaces
share an unrelated ancestor. Original `int` and `long` overloads keep every
compiler Code byte; only the owned bridge access bits are encoded.

Frozen callers, reflection, method handles and rebuilt callers observe argument
identity, aliases, wide bits, virtual callbacks, reentry and exact throwables.
Source and external-provider layouts compile every emitted Java unit and check
all original declarations and Code roles. Independent wrong programs qualify
the observer before decompilation; parent shadowing and inherited qualifiers
remain separate rejection checks.
